learning_outcomes.text: Students know the concepts of practical hardware development with abstract hardware description languages (VHDL) and the simulation of hardware circuits on FPGAs.
They master standard techniques of hardware-related processor development.
They are capable of implementing symmetric and asymmetric cryptosystems on modern FPGA systems.

syllabus_topics: Implementation of current cryptographic methods on practical hardware systems
Special hardware requirements like true random number generation (TRNG)
Efficient implementation of cryptosystems, especially regarding optimization for high speed, on modern FPGAs

assessment_methods.method: Bonus points from successful participation in exercises

assessment_rules: Credits are awarded for a passed exam. Up to 10 percent bonus points can be earned through successful participation in the exercises, which can be credited to the result of the module exam.
